lesson_title: Multiples Go Up, Factors Go In
hook_text: Juice in packs of 12, muffins in packs of 18. How few can you buy so they match exactly?
clip_script: Sports day in Mahikeng. Juice comes in packs of 12, muffins in packs of 18. Count up in 12s: 12, 24, 36. Count up in 18s: 18, 36. Match! 36 of each: 3 packs of juice, 2 packs of muffins. Those are multiples: they go up. Now 48 chairs in equal rows. 1 row of 48, 2 of 24, 3 of 16, 4 of 12, 6 of 8. Those are factors: they go in, in pairs. Stop when the pairs meet. 48 boys and 72 girls in equal teams? The biggest shared factor is 24. 24 teams, 2 boys and 3 girls each. Multiples go up, factors go in.
visual_style: Two skip-counting number lines lighting up at 36, then chairs snapping into rectangles of 1 by 48, 2 by 24, 3 by 16, 4 by 12 and 6 by 8.
mood: Puzzle-solving, like finding the missing piece.
pacing: Race the two skip-counts to the match, then build the chair rectangles one by one.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find all the factors of 60.
